questions.stem: You create a OneLake shortcut in a lakehouse that points to a folder in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. What happens to the data?

options.text: It is copied into OneLake every hour
It stays in ADLS Gen2 and is read in place through the shortcut
It is copied into OneLake once, when the shortcut is created
It is moved into OneLake and removed from ADLS Gen2

questions.explanation: A shortcut is a reference: the data stays where it is, and Fabric engines read it through OneLake without copying or moving it.

questions.stem: A lakehouse has a shortcut to a folder in another workspace's lakehouse. You delete the shortcut. What happens to the folder it pointed to?

options.text: The folder and its files are deleted along with it
Nothing: deleting a shortcut removes only the reference
The folder becomes read-only for its own lakehouse
The folder is moved into your lakehouse's Files section

questions.explanation: Deleting a shortcut deletes the shortcut object only. The target data is untouched.

questions.stem: Which three can a OneLake shortcut point to? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A Power BI report
A table in a Fabric deployment pipeline
Amazon S3
A folder in another Fabric lakehouse
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2

questions.explanation: Shortcuts can point to other OneLake locations and to external storage such as ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3 and Google Cloud Storage. A report or a deployment pipeline isn't storage.

questions.stem: A folder in ADLS Gen2 holds a Delta table. You want it to appear as a table that Spark and the SQL analytics endpoint can query. Where do you create the shortcut?

options.text: In the workspace, outside any lakehouse
At the top level of the lakehouse's Tables section
In the lakehouse's Files section, in any subfolder
In the warehouse's staging schema

questions.explanation: A shortcut at the top level of Tables to a Delta folder is discovered as a table. A shortcut under Files appears as a folder of files.

questions.stem: In a lakehouse, you try to create a shortcut to an external Delta table inside a subfolder of the Tables folder, and it isn't allowed. Where can you create it?

options.text: Only in a subfolder of the Tables folder named after the schema
Only in the Files folder, at the top level
Only in a KQL database Shortcuts folder
At the top level of the Tables folder

questions.explanation: Shortcuts in the Tables folder can be created only at the top level. In the Files folder, they can be created at any level.

questions.stem: A user who has delete permission in the target location deletes a file inside a lakehouse shortcut folder. What happens?

options.text: The whole shortcut is deleted, but the target is unchanged
Only the shortcut's view of the file is removed; the target file stays
The file is also deleted from the shortcut target
The delete fails because shortcuts are read-only

questions.explanation: Deleting the shortcut itself doesn't touch the target, but deleting a file or folder inside a shortcut deletes it in the target when the user has permission there.

questions.stem: A user reads data in Lakehouse A through a shortcut that points to Lakehouse B in another workspace, using Spark. Whose permissions does OneLake check on Lakehouse B?

options.text: The permissions of the user who created the shortcut
No permissions, because the shortcut grants access by itself
The workspace identity of the workspace that holds Lakehouse A
The calling user's permissions in Lakehouse B

questions.explanation: For OneLake shortcuts, OneLake uses the calling user's identity, and that user needs read permission in the target. The shortcut doesn't grant access on its own.

questions.stem: Notebooks in Fabric read the same files from an Amazon S3 shortcut many times a week, and the company wants to cut cross-cloud egress costs. Which statement about shortcut caching is true?

options.text: Cached files are kept for a fixed 90 days whatever their access
Individual files larger than 1 GB aren't cached
Caching is available only for ADLS Gen2 shortcuts
Caching is turned on per shortcut from the lakehouse explorer

questions.explanation: Caching supports S3, S3 compatible, GCS and gateway shortcuts, is enabled in Workspace settings on the OneLake tab, and keeps files 1-28 days, resetting on each access. Files over 1 GB aren't cached.

questions.stem: You create a shortcut named SalesShortcut in a KQL database. Which query reads its first 100 rows?

options.text: `SalesShortcut | take 100`
`materialized_view('SalesShortcut') | take 100`
`table('SalesShortcut') | take 100`
`external_table('SalesShortcut') | take 100`

questions.explanation: A KQL database treats shortcuts like external tables, so you query them with the external_table function.

questions.stem: Which two statements about OneLake shortcuts are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Internal shortcuts count toward the limit of 100 data source connections per item
Renaming the target folder updates every shortcut that points to it
A shortcut in the Tables folder whose name contains a space isn't recognized as a Delta table
Each Fabric item supports up to 100 shortcuts
Only users with permission on a cloud connection can create shortcuts that use that connection

questions.explanation: Binding a connection to a shortcut needs permission on the connection, and Delta doesn't support spaces in table names. Renaming a target can break a shortcut, the limit is 100,000 shortcuts per item, and internal shortcuts don't count toward the connection limit.
